answers.quote: In 1600, the East India Company acquired a charter from the ruler of England, Queen Elizabeth I, granting it the sole right to trade with the East.
answers.notes: Charter of 1600 from Queen Elizabeth I per c01.

answers.quote: The first English factory was set up on the banks of the river Hugli in 1651.
answers.notes: First English factory 1651 on banks of Hugli per c03.

answers.answer: ইংরেজ ও ফরাসি ইস্ট ইন্ডিয়া কোম্পানির মধ্যে
answers.quote: This conflict, popularly known as the Carnatic Wars, spanned a quarter century from 1744 to 1763. After reading this Unit you must have learned that the Anglo-French rivalry, talking the form of three Carnatic Wars constituted landmarks in the history of British conquest of south India in the 18th century. In order to establish their supremacy, it was necessary for the English EIC to eliminate the French from this region.
answers.notes: Carnatic Wars were the Anglo-French conflict per c39/c41.

answers.quote: in 1757, Robert Clive led the Company's army against Sirajuddaulah at Plassey. One of the main reasons for the defeat of the Nawab was that the forces led by Mir Jafar, one of Sirajuddaulah's commanders, never fought the battle. Clive had managed to secure his support by promising to make him nawab after crushing Sirajuddaulah.
answers.notes: Plassey fought in 1757 per c10 (also c48).

answers.quote: When Mir Jafar protested, the Company deposed him and installed Mir Qasim in his place. When Mir Qasim complained, he in turn was defeated in a battle fought at Buxar (1764), driven out of Bengal, and Mir Jafar was reinstalled.
answers.notes: Buxar dated 1764 in c12.

answers.quote: Finally, in 1765 the Mughal emperor appointed the Company as the Diwan of the provinces of Bengal. The Diwani allowed the Company to use the vast revenue resources of Bengal.
answers.notes: Diwani appointment in 1765 per c14 (also c50).

answers.quote: Tipu Sultan – The “Tiger of Mysore”
answers.notes: NCERT heading 'Tipu Sultan - The Tiger of Mysore' per c54.

answers.quote: Four wars were fought with Mysore (1767–69, 1780–84, 1790–92 and 1799). Only in the last – the Battle of Shrirangapatnam – did the Company ultimately win a victory. Tipu Sultan was killed defending his capital Shrirangapatnam
answers.notes: Tipu killed defending his capital Shrirangapatnam per c22.

answers.quote: The final wave of annexations occurred under Lord Dalhousie who was the Governor-General from 1848 to 1856. He devised a policy that came to be known as the Doctrine of Lapse. The doctrine declared that if an Indian ruler died without a male heir his kingdom would “lapse”, that is, become a part of Company territory.
answers.notes: Doctrine of Lapse devised by Dalhousie per c32.

answers.quote: One kingdom after another was annexed simply by applying this doctrine: Satara (1848), Sambalpur (1850), Udaipur (1852), Nagpur (1853) and Jhansi (1854).
answers.notes: Lapse list begins Satara (1848) per c33; also c46.

answers.quote: The firman or the imperial grant given by the Mughal emperor Farukshiyar in 1717 gave duty free concession only to the Company's imports and exports and not to the Company servants' private trade. The misuse of this trade privilege by the Company officials for private trade meant a heavy loss to the Nawabs treasury.
answers.notes: 1717 firman by Farrukhsiyar per c47.

answers.quote: By 1696, it began building a fort around the settlement. Two years later, it bribed Mughal officials into giving the Company zamindari rights over three villages. One of these was Kalikata, which later grew into the city of Calcutta or Kolkata as it is known today.
answers.notes: Kalikata grew into Calcutta per c04.

answers.quote: The decisive battle of the third Carnatic War was Fought at Wandiwash on 22 January 1760. General Eyre Coote's army totally routed the French army under Lally.
answers.notes: Wandiwash was decisive battle of Third Carnatic War per c40.

answers.answer: ক্লাইভ তাঁকে সিরাজকে হারানোর পর নবাব করার প্রতিশ্রুতি দিয়েছিলেন
answers.quote: in 1757, Robert Clive led the Company's army against Sirajuddaulah at Plassey. One of the main reasons for the defeat of the Nawab was that the forces led by Mir Jafar, one of Sirajuddaulah's commanders, never fought the battle. Clive had managed to secure his support by promising to make him nawab after crushing Sirajuddaulah.
answers.notes: Clive promised to make Mir Jafar nawab per c10.

answers.answer: মুঘল সম্রাট দ্বিতীয় শাহ আলম ও অবধের নবাব সুজাউদ্দৌলা
answers.quote: Mir Kasim was successful in forming a confederacy with the Emperor Shah Alam-II and Nawab Shuja-ud-daula of Awadh against the British. The battle of Buxar gave them the complete political control over Bengal. Actually, the process of transition started with the battle of Plassey and culminated in the battle of Buxar.
answers.notes: Mir Kasim's confederacy with Shah Alam-II and Shuja-ud-daula per c49.

answers.quote: shifting the capital from Murshidabad to Monghyr in Bihar in order to keep a safe distance from the Company at Calcutta, and re-organising the bureaucracy by the men of his own choice and remodelling the army to enhance its skill and efficiency.
answers.notes: Capital shifted Murshidabad to Monghyr in Bihar per c51.

answers.quote: According to the terms of this alliance, Indian rulers were not allowed to have their independent armed forces. They were to be protected by the Company, but had to pay for the “subsidiary forces” that the Company was supposed to maintain for the purpose of this protection. If the Indian rulers failed to make the payment, then part of their territory was taken away as penalty.
answers.notes: Rulers had to pay for subsidiary forces per c18.

answers.answer: রাজ্যের অর্ধেকের বেশি অংশ কোম্পানিকে ছেড়ে দিতে হয়
answers.quote: when Richard Wellesley was Governor-General (1798–1805), the Nawab of Awadh was forced to give over half of his territory to the Company in 1801, as he failed to pay for the “subsidiary forces”. Hyderabad was also forced to cede territories on similar grounds.
answers.notes: Awadh forced to give over half its territory in 1801 per c19.

answers.quote: With their defeat in the Third Battle of Panipat in 1761, the Marathas' dream of ruling from Delhi was shattered.
answers.notes: Dream of ruling from Delhi shattered at Panipat 1761 per c26.

answers.quote: In the first war that ended in 1782 with the Treaty of Salbai, there was no clear victor. The Second Anglo-Maratha War (1803–05) was fought on different fronts, resulting in the British gaining Orissa and the territories north of the Yamuna river including Agra and Delhi. Finally, the Maratha power came to end with the Third Anglo-Maratha War of 1817–19. The Peshwa was removed and sent away to Bithur near Kanpur with a pension.
answers.notes: First Maratha war ended 1782 with Treaty of Salbai per c27.

answers.quote: in 1792, attacked by the combined forces of the Marathas, the Nizam of Hyderabad and the Company, Tipu was forced to sign a treaty with the British by which two of his sons were taken away as hostages.
answers.notes: Two of Tipu's sons taken as hostages in 1792 per c23.

answers.quote: Under Lord Hastings (Governor-General from 1813 to 1823), a new policy of “paramountcy” was initiated. Now the Company claimed that its authority was paramount or supreme, hence its power was greater than that of Indian states.
answers.notes: Paramountcy began under Lord Hastings 1813-1823 per c28.

answers.quote: They fought a prolonged war with Afghanistan between 1838 and 1842, and established indirect Company rule there. Sind was taken over in 1843.
answers.notes: Sind taken over in 1843 per c30.

answers.quote: the presence of Maharaja Ranjit Singh held back the Company. After his death in 1839, two prolonged wars were fought with the Sikh kingdom. Ultimately, in 1849, Punjab was annexed.
answers.notes: Punjab annexed in 1849 per c31 (also c43).

answers.quote: One kingdom after another was annexed simply by applying this doctrine: Satara (1848), Sambalpur (1850), Udaipur (1852), Nagpur (1853) and Jhansi (1854).
answers.notes: Jhansi (1854) in Lapse list per c33; also c46.

The misuse of this trade privilege by the Company officials for private trade meant a heavy loss to the Nawabs treasury.
answers.notes: 1717 firman covered only Company imports/exports, not servants' private trade, per c47.

answers.answer: ইউরোপে ইংরেজ-ফরাসি শত্রুতার সূত্রপাত, যা ভারতে ছড়িয়ে পড়ে
answers.quote: The First Carnatic War was provoked by the outbreak of hostilities in Europe in 1742 between the two countries. By 1745 the war spread to India where French and English East India Companies were rivals in trade and political influence.
answers.notes: First Carnatic War provoked by European hostilities spreading to India per c41.

answers.answer: ব্রিটেন থেকে সোনা-রূপা এনে পণ্য কেনার প্রয়োজন পুরোপুরি শেষ হয়ে যায়
answers.quote: The outflow of gold from Britain slowed after the Battle of Plassey, and entirely stopped after the assumption of Diwani. Now revenues from India could finance Company expenses.
answers.notes: Gold outflow from Britain entirely stopped after Diwani per c15.

answers.quote: So English victory in the battle field of Plassey, (June, 1757) was decided before the battle was fought. It was not the superiority of the military power but the conspiracy of the Nawab's officials that helped the English in winning the battle.
answers.notes: IGNOU: conspiracy of Nawab's officials, not military superiority, per c48.

answers.quote: After the Battle of Buxar (1764), the Company appointed Residents in Indian states. They were political or commercial agents and their job was to serve and further the interests of the Company.
answers.notes: Residents appointed after Buxar per c17.

answers.answer: তাঁর বন্দর দিয়ে চন্দনকাঠ, গোলমরিচ ও এলাচ রপ্তানি বন্ধ করে দেন
answers.quote: In 1785, Tipu Sultan stopped the export of sandalwood, pepper and cardamom through the ports of his kingdom, and disallowed local merchants from trading with the Company. He also established a close relationship with the French in India, and modernised his army with their help.
answers.notes: Tipu stopped export of sandalwood, pepper, cardamom in 1785 per c21.

answers.answer: ওয়াদিয়ার বংশকে সিংহাসনে বসিয়ে অধীনতামূলক মৈত্রী চাপিয়ে দেওয়া হয়
answers.quote: Mysore was placed under the former ruling dynasty of the Wodeyars and a subsidiary alliance was imposed on the state.
answers.notes: Mysore placed under Wodeyars, subsidiary alliance imposed, per c24.

answers.answer: ১৮২৪ সালে গ্রেপ্তার হন এবং ১৮২৯ সালে কারাগারে মারা যান
answers.quote: when the British tried to annex the small state of Kitoor (in Karnataka today), Rani Channamma took to arms and led an anti-British resistance movement. She was arrested in 1824 and died in prison in 1829.
answers.notes: Rani Channamma arrested 1824, died in prison 1829, per c29.

answers.answer: জলন্ধর দোয়াব ব্রিটিশরা সংযুক্ত করে এবং লাহোরে ব্রিটিশ সৈন্য মোতায়েন হয়
answers.quote: the first war between the Company and the Punjab was declared on 13 December 1845. Because of such failure of leadership, the formidable Punjab army was defeated in a series of encounters and was forced to sign the humiliating treaty of Lahore on 8 March, 1846. The British annexed the Jalandhar Doab
answers.notes: Jalandhar Doab annexation after Lahore treaty directly in c44; the Lahore troop-deployment clause is not stated in the claims, so confidence LIKELY not SURE.

answers.quote: Finally, in 1856, the Company also took over Awadh. This time the British had an added argument – they said they were “obliged by duty” to take over Awadh in order to free the people from the “misgovernment” of the Nawab!
answers.notes: British argued duty to free people from Nawab's misgovernment per c34 (also c46).
